name: Week 0 · Get Ready
headline: Are we ready to start on our own data?
outcome: Your accounts, operator, baseline and data pack, ready before the first build on Dec 2.
outputs: Intake in and operator named
AI Brain set up and time baseline recorded
Readiness gate checked on the practice set
notes: Week 1 goes fastest when your accounts work, your operator is named and your data is in one place. None of this is hard. It just has to happen before Dec 2, not during the first build. Owner: Name your operator, fill in the intake and set up your own AI Brain. Protect a weekly time for the operating review. Operator: Check access, gather the data pack, set up the working folder and run the readiness exercise. Time: owner about 45 to 60 minutes. Operator about 2 to 3 hours, when your data is easy to reach. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-0.

checklist.text: Fill in the intake and name your operator
checklist.hint: Your intake form arrives with your welcome email.

checklist.text: Watch the orientation
checklist.hint: About 30 minutes.

checklist.text: Open AI Brain Setup and finish its guided setup
checklist.hint: It’s free. The prompts stay on its Library page.

checklist.text: Record your time baseline with The Ops Time Audit
checklist.hint: Report prep, meeting prep, follow-up admin and one agent task.

checklist.text: Gather the data pack
checklist.hint: Usable data, not perfect data. The minimum is fine.

checklist.text: Run the readiness exercise on the practice set
checklist.hint: Find the input that’s missing on purpose.

name: Week 1 · Know the Business
headline: What are we paying for leads, and what can we trust?
outcome: A checked view of what your leads cost by source, with every unknown named.
outputs: Production totals tied to their source report
A worksheet for at least one source, unknowns named
One decision or a dated data-repair assignment
notes: Before you change spend or push agents, you need to tell production, revenue, acquisition cost, contribution and data uncertainty apart. We start with checked spend and lead counts, then go only as far as the data supports. Owner: Review the exceptions at a fixed weekly time. Decide what you can conclude, what you can’t yet, and what you’d need to know. Operator: Refresh the weekly numbers view and fill in the worksheet. Refresh source economics monthly, after the books close. Time: owner about 2 to 2.5 hours, including the 90-minute build and real use. Operator about 3 to 4 hours, including the build, practice, refreshing inputs and office hours if you need them. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-1.

name: Week 2 · Own the Day
headline: What needs attention, and who owns the next action?
outcome: A ten-minute morning brief where every action has an owner, a date and a source.
outputs: A saved brief and one checked run
One task destination, no duplicate board
Five uses and one reconciled meeting-to-task run
notes: The goal isn’t a prettier summary. It’s fewer commitments with nobody’s name on them. You get one consistent way to decide what deserves your attention each morning. Owner: Review the brief for ten minutes. Accept only tasks with a named owner, a due date and a definition of done. Operator: Refresh the inputs at a fixed time: the Week 1 numbers view, the task list and one authorized meeting or email thread. Time: owner about 2 to 2.5 hours, including the 90-minute build and real use. Operator about 3 to 4 hours, including the build, practice, refreshing inputs and office hours if you need them. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-2.

name: Week 3 · Turn Insight into a Decision
headline: What should we solve this week?
outcome: A meeting packet that ends in a recorded decision, with an owner and a date.
outputs: A usable agenda and one evidence-backed issue
A decision log, “no action” decisions included
One real meeting with owned follow-through
notes: A report is only worth something if it changes a decision or a behavior. This should shorten your meeting prep and sharpen the issues you discuss. It shouldn’t add a meeting. Owner: Pick the highest-priority issue and make the call. AI can help frame options. It doesn’t make the decision. Operator: Prepare the packet the day before your existing leadership meeting, from the Week 1 numbers, the Week 2 commitments and the issue list. Time: owner about 2 to 2.5 hours, including the 90-minute build and real use. Operator about 3 to 4 hours, including the build, practice, refreshing inputs and office hours if you need them. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-3.

name: Week 4 · Protect the Pipeline
headline: Where is execution slipping?
outcome: A ranked list of where deals are slipping, each with a record reference and a next step.
outputs: A ranked exception list with record references
A disposition and an owner for the top five
A rerun showing what’s still open
notes: The point is to send attention to the gaps, not to restate every record in your CRM. A missing update isn’t the same as a stalled deal. The review has to tell them apart. Owner: Before your pipeline review, confirm the exceptions with the responsible agents and record a next action for each. Operator: Run the review before your existing pipeline meeting. Start with active deals and one small priority segment. Time: owner about 2 to 2.5 hours, including the 90-minute build and real use. Operator about 3 to 4 hours, including the build, practice, refreshing inputs and office hours if you need them. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-4.

name: Week 5 · Coach from Evidence
headline: What behavior should change for this agent?
outcome: A coaching packet that keeps facts, hypotheses and questions apart, and one agreed behavior to change.
outputs: One checked packet and three diagnostic questions
One proposed behavior experiment
Two real conversations with follow-up dates
notes: Missing activity, weak conversion, a bad process and incomplete tracking all look alike on a scorecard. Coaching depends on telling them apart. AI helps you prepare a better conversation. It doesn’t judge people. Owner: Before the 1:1, verify the numbers. In it, ask about context, agree on one behavior to change and set the next review date. Operator: Prepare the packet from agreed activity definitions, production context, prior commitments and the agent’s own perspective. Time: owner about 2 to 2.5 hours, including the 90-minute build and real use. Operator about 3 to 4 hours, including the build, practice, refreshing inputs and office hours if you need them. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-5.

name: Week 6 · Delegate an Outcome
headline: What work can leave the owner’s desk without lowering standards?
outcome: One recurring deliverable off the owner’s desk, with a responsibility card and a review checklist.
outputs: A responsibility card from your playbook
A tested first draft and a review checklist
One real cycle accepted by the owner
notes: A task that says “handle this” doesn’t define quality or who decides. AI can draft the work. A person still owns the result and knows when to escalate. Owner: Define the outcome, the boundaries and the acceptance standard. Then accept or return the first cycle against the checklist. Operator: Run it, or hand it to the team member who now owns it. Check the draft and submit it through your existing approval process. Time: owner about 2 to 2.5 hours, including the 90-minute build and real use. Operator about 3 to 4 hours, including the build, practice, refreshing inputs and office hours if you need them. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-6.

name: Week 7 · Make the Workflow Repeatable
headline: Can our operator adapt and run the next workflow without the instructor?
outcome: A versioned onboarding skill your operator can explain, test and repair without the instructor.
outputs: A versioned skill with three passing tests
A runbook a second person can follow
A handoff, or “tested and ready” if there’s no hire yet
notes: This is how you scale what feels unscalable: write down how your team brings someone up to standard, and keep the human coaching and decisions. It’s also the independence test. Your team should be able to explain it, test it and fix it without us. Owner: Supply the approved role, standards and resources. Review the plan and assign every checkpoint to a real person. Operator: Adapt the supplied plan, run the three tests, write the runbook and hand it to a second person to rerun. Time: owner about 2 to 2.5 hours, including the 90-minute build and real use. Operator about 3 to 4 hours, including the build, practice, refreshing inputs and office hours if you need them. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-7.

name: Week 8 · Sustain and Expand
headline: What stays, what stops, and what should agents adopt next?
outcome: A cohort-end review: what stays, what stops, and a 90-day plan your team runs without us.
outputs: An evidence-backed scorecard
Keep, fix or retire for each workflow
A 90-day plan and an agent go or no-go
notes: This week keeps the work from fading once the cohort ends. It’s also where you decide what not to scale. That’s just as useful. Owner: Make the keep, fix or retire call on each workflow, sign the 90-day plan and make a real go or no-go on agent rollout. Operator: Gather the logs and outputs from Weeks 1 to 7, rerun the Week 1 numbers on the same definitions and assemble the review. Time: owner about 2 to 2.5 hours, including the 90-minute build and real use. Operator about 3 to 4 hours, including the build, practice, refreshing inputs and office hours if you need them. These are planning estimates, not guarantees. The full week, with the live build, office hours, homework, evidence packet and rubric, is at /course/week-8.
